       \approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}
       \approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1$,
$ f^{*}_{0.95}-1\approx22$,

so that $\mu^{2}_{L}=[\sqrt f-1.645]^{2}>10$ and hence
$R_{U}\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$ with $95\%$ one-sided confidence.
With the usual two-sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation this is
$[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$, the familiar $22\!-\!26$ range.
In the $1/F$ mean-bias shorthand this is the $F\approx10\!-\!11$ 
Nagar point rule lifted to the $95\%$ lower confidence bound for
$\mu^{2}$.

Remark.  On the conventional size-corrected Stock–Yogo test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$ the $5\%$ critical value is
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, i.e. the $95\%$ quantile of 
$\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$.  That is
$c_{SY}(k_{2}=1,10\%)\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$, the
$F\gtrsim16$ table value normally quoted as the $10\%$ maximal
relative Nagar bias rule, the $F>10$ mean-bias rule made $5\%$ size
correct. The $ \approx23$ number above is the literal $95\%$ one-sided
lower confidence bound $\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the
concentration parameter, i.e. the $F\approx10$ point rule inflated by
the sampling error in the first stage $F$.

18.text:
For the homoscedastic just identified model with $k_{2}=1$

${\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]\approx 
\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{v}^{-2}k_{2}\mu^{-2}$ , 
${\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]=\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{v}^{-2}$,

$R(\mu^{2})\equiv {\rm RelBias}\approx k_{2}\mu^{-2}\approx\mu^{-2}$,
$ {\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ , $F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$.

In weak instrument asymptotics

$F_{1}\approx\bigl(Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}\bigr)^{2}$ , $Z\sim N(0,1)$,
$\sqrt{F_{1}}\approx\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z$ ,
i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\sim N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ to first order.

Put $R_{0}=0.10$.  On the Nagar scale $R_{0}=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}$,

$\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$, $\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx3.16$.

For an observed $f$ a one-sided $1-\alpha$ lower bound for
$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}\simeq\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$.

Hence a $1-\alpha$ upper bound for the Nagar relative bias is

$R_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}\simeq\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{-2}$.

$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e.

$\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

$\;f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}\;.$

With the one-sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Big]^{2}
       \approx(3.162+1.645)^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx 23.1$ .

That is $F-1\approx22$, $F\approx 22\!-\!24$ on the
$\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ normalisation, $ \approx 26$
with the conventional two-sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$.  In the point mean
Nagar shorthand $R\simeq1/F$ this is the familiar $F\approx10\!-\!11$
rule lifted to a $95\%$ lower confidence bound for the concentration
parameter.

On the usual Stock–Yogo size-corrected test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$ the $5\%$ critical value is the
$0.95$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, $c_{SY}\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,

i.e. the conventional $F\gtrsim16$ $10\%$ maximal relative bias
reference, the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct.  The
$ \approx23$ value above is the literal $95\%$ one-sided lower
confidence bound $\mu_{L}^{2}=[\sqrt F-z_{0.95}]^{2}\ge10$ for the
concentration parameter, $\approx16.4$ on the Stock–Yogo $5\%$ size
calibration. ∎

15.text:
With $k_{2}=1$ the homoskedastic Nagar first order relative bias is

${\rm RelBias}_{N}\simeq \frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}}\simeq \mu^{-2}$ ,
${\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ ,
$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$ .

In weak instrument asymptotics

$\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\qquad Z\sim N(0,1)$,
i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$.

On a point estimate
${\rm RelBias}_{N}\approx1/F_{1}$ and
${\rm RelBias}_{N}=0.10\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/0.10=10$,
${\rm E}F_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}=11$, the familiar $F\approx10$ mean-bias rule.

For an observed $f$ a $1-\alpha$ one-sided lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$
on the $\sqrt F$ normal scale is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$ ,
so that on the Nagar scale

${\rm RelBias}_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)=\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{-2}$ .

${\rm RelBias}_{U}(f)\le0.10$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge10$ i.e.

$\sqrt f\ge \sqrt{10}+z_{1-\alpha}$ .

Hence the $1-\alpha$ lower confidence inversion on the $\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$
limit is

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2},
\qquad \mu_{0}^{2}=10.$

With the usual one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
      \approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}
      \approx4.81^{2}\approx 23.1$,

i.e. $f-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, 
$F\gtrsim22\!-\!24$ in round numbers.  With the conventional two sided
$z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$.

This is the literal $95\%$ one-sided lower confidence bound
$\mu_{L}^{2}=[\sqrt F-z_{0.95}]^{2}>10$ for the Nagar concentration
parameter, i.e. the $1/F$ rule $F\approx10$ lifted to a $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$.  In the conventional size-controlled
Stock–Yogo testing form $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$ the $5\%$ size
critical value is the $95\%$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,

$c_{SY,10\%,k=1}=q_{0.95}\!\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\big]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17,$

the $F>10$ mean bias rule made $5\%$ size correct and the value quoted
in practice as the $10\%$ maximal relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias threshold.
The $ \approx23$ figure above is the normal $\sqrt F$ $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself, the $ \approx16.4$ figure the
usual Stock–Yogo $5\%$ size corrected critical value. ∎

4.text:
For a just identified homoskedastic first stage the Nagar first order
relative bias is

${\rm RelBias}\equiv 
\frac{E[\hat \beta_{2SLS}-\beta]}{{\rm plim}[\hat \beta_{OLS}-\beta]}
\approx \frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}},\qquad k_{2}=1$,

and in the weak instrument limit with $\nu_{2}\to\infty$

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2}),\qquad 
\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1)$,

so that $E[F_{1}]=1+\mu^{2}$ and on the mean scale
${\rm RelBias}\approx\mu^{-2}\approx(F_{1}-1)^{-1}\approx F_{1}^{-1}$.
The point Nagar $10\%$ bias boundary is

$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}\iff \mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10,$
$E[F_{1}]_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}\approx 11$,

the familiar $F\approx10$ mean-bias rule.

Let $f$ be the observed first stage.  On the $\sqrt F$ normalisation

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}\approx \sqrt f -Z$,

so that a one sided $1-\alpha$ lower confidence bound for
$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)\approx\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu^{2}_{L}(f)\approx\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{2}$,
and

$R_{U}(f)\approx \mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e.

$\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}$,
$\sqrt{f^{*}}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$.

Hence on the $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ normal approximation

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\approx\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}$.

With $\mu_{0}^{2}=10$ and the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile
$z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\Big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Big]^{2}
\approx\bigl[3.162+1.645\bigr]^{2}
\approx4.81^{2}\approx 23\,{\rm -}\,24$,

$ f^{*}-1\approx22$, i.e. $F-1>10$ with $95\%$ one sided lower
confidence for $\mu^{2}$.  With the usual two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$
this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$, the $22\!-\!26$ range
usually quoted for the literal $95\%$ lower confidence bound
$\mu^{2}_{L}>10\iff R_{U}<0.10$.  The point mean rule is
$R\approx 1/F<0.10\iff F\approx10\!-\!11$.

Remark.  In test form the $5\%$ size weak instrument test of
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$ is
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, i.e. $c$ is the $95\%$ quantile of
$\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$.  The Stock–Yogo size corrected critical value is

$c_{SY,10\%}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38
\approx16\!-\!17$,

the $F\approx16$ value normally quoted in the literature as the
$95\%$ size/$10\%$ maximal relative Nagar bias threshold, the
$F>10$ point rule lifted to the conventional $5\%$ size calibration.
This is the $F\approx16.4$ Stock–Yogo table value that is used in
practice, the normal $\sqrt F$ inversion above being the
conservative $95\%$ lower confidence bound $\approx23$ for the
concentration parameter itself. ∎

6.text:
In the homoskedastic just identified case $k_{2}=1$

${\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]\approx \sigma_{uv}\sigma_{vv}^{-1}\mu^{-2}$,
${\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]=\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{vv}^{-1}$
so that to Nagar first order

$R(\mu^{2})\equiv\frac{{\rm Bias}_{2SLS}}{{\rm Bias}_{OLS}}
\approx\frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}}\approx\frac1{\mu^{2}}\approx\frac1{F-1}
\approx\frac1F$,

$E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ and in the weak instrument limit

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2}),\qquad
 \sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1),$

i.e. $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$.  With the point Nagar
boundary

$R_{0}=0.10\iff \mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10 ,$

$E F_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}=11$, the familiar $F\approx10$ mean bias rule.

A $1-\alpha$ one sided lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ from an observed
$f$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,

so that on the Nagar scale
$R_{U}(f)\approx \mu_{L}^{-2}(f)=\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{-2}$.
Requiring $R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ i.e. $\mu_{L}^{2}\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ gives the
normal inversion

$\sqrt{f^{*}}=\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{2}$.

With the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
\approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1$,

i.e. $F-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, $F\gtrsim
22\!-\!24$ on the $\sqrt{F}\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ weak instrument
normalisation.  With the conventional two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ this
is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$.  On the $F-1$ mean correction
$\sqrt{F-1}\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ this is $F^{*}\approx
\big[\sqrt{10}+z_{0.95}\big]^{2}+1\approx24$, the usual $F\approx
23\!-\!26$ $95\%$ one sided lower confidence bound for the
concentration parameter, i.e. the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule lifted
to a $95\%$ lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$.

In particular the point Nagar mean requirement is $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff
F\gtrsim10\!-\!11$.  The conventional size corrected weak instrument
test

$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$,

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}\!\left[F>c\right]=0.05,$

is the Stock–Yogo $5\%$ size test.  On the non-central limit
$F\mid\mu^{2}=10\to\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$

$c_{0.05}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx
16\!-\!17$,

the familiar Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical value
for $k_{2}=1$, the $F>10$ mean rule made $5\%$ size correct.  This is
the $F\approx16$ value normally quoted in applied work, the $23$
value above being the strict $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ $95\%$
lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself. ∎

20.text:
In the homoskedastic just identified case $k_{2}=1$

${\rm E}\big[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta\big]\simeq \sigma_{uv}\sigma_{vv}^{-1}
k_{2}\mu^{-2}$ , ${\rm plim}\big[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta\big]=
\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{vv}^{-1}$,

so that to Nagar first order

$R(\mu^{2})\equiv 
\frac{{\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]}
     {{\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]}\simeq\frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}} ,
\qquad  {\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2} ,$

$R\simeq\mu^{-2}\simeq(F-1)^{-1}\simeq F^{-1}$ in the usual $1/F$
shorthand.  On weak instrument asymptotics

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi_{1}^{2}(\mu^{2})$, 
$\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1)$,

so that $ \sqrt{\mu^{2}}\approx \sqrt F-Z$.  For an observed $f$ a
one sided $1-\alpha$ lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)\approx \sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,

and on the Nagar scale $R_{U}(f)\simeq \mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.
The $10\%$ Nagar boundary is

$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$,
$\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\simeq3.16$,

the familiar $E F_{0}\simeq1+\mu_{0}^{2}\simeq11$, i.e. the $F\approx10$
mean bias rule $R\simeq1/F<0.10$.

$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ i.e. $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ is

$\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}$,
$\sqrt{f^{*}_{1-\alpha}}=\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

i.e.

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\,\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\,\Big]^{2}$.

With the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Big]^{2}
\simeq\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}\simeq4.81^{2}\simeq23.1$,

$ f^{*}-1\simeq22$, i.e. $F\gtrsim22\!-\!24$ on the $\sqrt F\approx
N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ weak instrument normalisation, $F\gtrsim26.2$ on
the conventional two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation
$[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}$.  In particular
$\mu_{L}^{2}= \big[\sqrt F-1.645\big]^{2}>10$ gives
$R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$ with $95\%$ one sided confidence,
the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule lifted to the $F\approx23$ $95\%$
lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter.  On the
$F-1$ mean scale this is the usual $F\approx11$ point rule,
$R\simeq1/F$.

Remark.  In the usual size-corrected weak instrument testing
formulation $H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$ is rejected at $5\%$ size
when $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$.  On the $F_{1,\infty}(\mu^{2})$
limit this is the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical
value

$c_{SY,10\%,k=1}=q_{0.95}\!\big[\chi_{1}^{2}(10)\big]
\simeq16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,

the $F\approx10$ mean Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct and the
value conventionally quoted in the tables as the $95\%$ confidence/
$10\%$ maximal relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias threshold.  This is the
$F\approx16.4$ operative Stock–Yogo calibration, the $23$ above being
the strict $\sqrt F-z$ $95\%$ lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$
itself. ∎

public_text.2:
For the just identified homoskedastic case the Nagar first order relative bias is

R ≈ k2/μ² ,  k2=1 ,    E[F]≈1+μ²

so on a mean basis R≈1/(F-1)≈1/F and the point 10% rule is μ²0=k2/0.10=10,
E[F]0≈11, the familiar F≈10 rule.

The operative “95% confidence that the asymptotic relative bias is <10%” is the usual weak-instrument testing formulation

H0 : R ≥0.10 ⇔ H0 : μ² ≤ μ²0 = k2/0.10 =10
vs H1 : μ²>10,

rejected at 5% size when F exceeds the 95% quantile of the first stage F under the boundary μ²0.  Under weak instrument asymptotics with ν2→∞

F1 →d χ²1(μ²),  F1 ≈ [Z+√μ²]² , Z∼N(0,1),

so the size-corrected critical value c0.10 solves

P_{μ²=10}[ F1>c0.10 ] =0.05 ⇔ P_{μ²=10}[ χ²1(10) > c0.10 ]=0.05 .

That is the 95th percentile of a non-central χ²1 with non-centrality 10, i.e. the Stock–Yogo 10% maximal relative bias critical value for k2=1. Numerically

c0.10 = q0.95[ χ²1(10) ] ≈ 16.38,

the tabulated Stock–Yogo value.  An observed F>c0.10 rejects μ²≤10 at the conventional 5% level, which is the 95% confidence /5% size statement that the Nagar asymptotic relative bias is <10% that is used in practice.

The √F≈N(√μ²,1) inversion √f* = √10+z0.95 giving f*≈[√10+1.645]²≈23.1 is a 95% lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter itself, √μ²L=√f−z0.95, and then plugging that bound into R≈1/μ².  It is a confidence interval for μ² followed by a point transformation, i.e. a Bonferroni-type lower bound on μ². It double counts sampling variation in the first stage F because the first stage F is already the test statistic for μ². The size-corrected test inverts P(F>c|μ²=10)=0.05 once, not √μ²L=(√F−z)²≥10.

Hence on the Nagar/Stock–Yogo calibration that is used for the 10% maximal relative 2SLS/OLS bias the 5% size-corrected threshold for one instrument is the familiar Stock–Yogo value

F*≈16.38≈16–17,

conventionally quoted as F≳16.  That is the F>10 point rule lifted to the usual 5% weak-instrument testing size. The ≈23 value is the much more conservative normal-delta lower confidence bound for μ² itself, not the Stock–Yogo size-corrected critical value for the hypothesis H0:R≥0.10.
public_text.13:
The 95% confidence statement that is used in the weak-instrument literature is the size-corrected Stock–Yogo test of the Nagar boundary, not a delta-method lower confidence interval for μ² that is then plugged into R≈k/μ².

With k2=1, homoscedastic Nagar first order

E[β̂2SLS-β]≈σ_uv/σ_v² k2/μ² ,  plim[β̂OLS-β]=σ_uv/σ_v²

so that

R(μ²)≡Bias2SLS/BiasOLS≈k2/μ²≈1/(EF-1)≈1/F .

The point boundary R0=0.10 is μ²0=k2/R0=10, i.e. EF≈11, the familiar F≈10 mean-bias rule.

The operational “95% confident that R<0.10” is the usual weak-instrument test

H0 : R≥0.10 ⇔ μ²≤μ²0=10   vs   H1 : μ²>10,

rejected at 5% size when F1>c with

P_{μ²=10}[F1>c]=0.05 .

With ν2→∞, F1→d χ²1(μ²) and the 5% critical value is the 95th percentile of χ²1(10).  That is the Stock–Yogo size-corrected critical value,

c0.10 = Q0.95[χ²1(10)] ≈ 16.38 ≈ 16–17,

the published 10% maximal relative-bias critical value for k2=1.  An observed F>c therefore rejects μ²≤10 at the conventional 5% level, i.e. in the usual weak-instrument testing sense we can say with 95% confidence that the Nagar asymptotic relative bias is <10%.

The √F≈N(√μ²,1) inversion √μ²L=√f−z0.95 and the requirement μ²L≥10 gives √f* =√10+z0.95 and f*≈(√10+1.645)²≈23.1.  That is a 95% lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter itself, √μ²L=√F−z, and then a point transformation R≈1/μ². It double counts sampling variation: the first stage F is already the test statistic for μ². The Stock–Yogo calibration already incorporates the sampling distribution of F under the boundary μ²=10 via P(F>c|μ²=10)=0.05. Imposing μ²L=(√F−z)²≥10 on top of that is a Bonferroni-type bound for μ² and is conservative relative to the size-corrected test that is actually used.

Hence on the Nagar/Stock–Yogo calibration that is used in practice the 10% maximal relative bias threshold for one instrument is the 5% size corrected value EF≈1+10 and c≈16.4.  In round numbers this is the conventional F≳16 rule, essentially F≈16, the F>10 point rule lifted to the 5% size Stock–Yogo version. ∎
public_text.5:
The Nagar first-order relative bias for the just identified homoskedastic case with $k_{2}=1$ is

${\rm RelBias}\simeq k_{2}/\mu^{2}\simeq 1/(E F-1)\simeq 1/F$,

$E F=1+\mu^{2}$ and in the weak-instrument limit $F_{1}\to^{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$. 
The $10\%$ maximal relative bias point is $\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/0.10=10$, i.e. $E F_{0}\simeq11$, the familiar $F>10$ mean rule.

The operational $95\%$ confidence statement in the weak-instrument literature is the Stock-Yogo size-corrected test

$H_{0}:{\rm RelBias}\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le\mu_{0}^{2}=10$

vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$, rejected at $5\%$ size when $F$ exceeds the $95\%$ quantile of the first-stage distribution under the boundary $\mu^{2}=10$.

With $\nu_{2}\to\infty$

$\Pr_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05\iff\Pr_{\mu^{2}=10}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)>c]=0.05$,

i.e. $c$ is the $95\%$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$, the $5\%$ critical value of $F_{1,\infty}(10)$. Numerically

$c_{0.10}=q_{0.95}\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\big]\approx 16.38$,

the published Stock-Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical value for $k_{2}=1$. An observed $F>c_{0.10}$ rejects $\mu^{2}\le10$ at $5\%$ and, on the Nagar approximation, is the conventional $95\%$ size-corrected statement that the asymptotic relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias is $<10\%$.

The $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ inversion $\sqrt f_{*}=\sqrt{10}+z_{0.95}$ giving $f_{*}\approx(\sqrt{10}+1.645)^{2}\approx23.1$ is a $1-\alpha$ lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter itself, $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$, and then plugging that bound into $R\approx1/\mu^{2}$. That is a bound on $\mu^{2}$ and then a point transformation, i.e. a Bonferroni-type confidence interval for $\mu^{2}$. It double counts the sampling variation already present in $F$ and is more conservative than the size-corrected test of $H_{0}:R\ge0.10$.

In practice the $F>10$ point Nagar rule is lifted to the $5\%$ size-corrected Stock-Yogo rule $F\gtrsim16.38$. In round numbers that is $F\approx16$, the usual weak-instrument threshold for a $10\%$ maximal relative Nagar bias with one instrument. ∎
public_text.7:
The just identified homoskedastic Nagar first-order relative bias is

R ≈ k2/μ² ,  k2=1,      E[F] ≈1+μ²,    R≈1/(F-1)≈1/F

Under the homoskedastic Nagar first order with $k_{2}=1$

${\rm RelBias}\approx R(\mu^{2}) =k_{2}/\mu^{2}\approx\mu^{-2}$,
$E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$  and in the weak instrument limit

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi_{1}^{2}(\mu^{2})$,  $\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1)$,
$Z\sim N(0,1)$.

Hence on the $\sqrt F$ scale

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}\approx \sqrt{F}-Z$,

so that a $1-\alpha$ one sided asymptotic lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$
from an observed $f$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)\approx\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\approx\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{2}$.

On the Nagar scale $R_{U}(f)\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.  The $10\%$ Nagar
boundary is

$R_{0}=0.10\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$,

so that $R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ i.e.

$\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$.

Hence the $1-\alpha$ lower confidence inversion on the $\sqrt F\approx
N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ normalisation is

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\approx\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}$,
$\mu_{0}^{2}=10$.

With the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
\approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1$,

i.e. $f^{*}-1\approx22$ on the $F-1\approx\mu^{2}$ normalisation,
$F\approx22\!-\!24$, about $F\approx23$ on the usual $\sqrt F$ normal
weak instrument approximation and $F^{*}\approx(\sqrt{10}+1.96)^{2}\approx
26.2$ with the conventional two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation.
Neglecting the sampling error in $F$ this is the familiar point Nagar
rule $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff F\gtrsim10\!-\!11$, $EF\approx11$.

In particular $R\simeq1/F$ gives the point mean rule $F\approx10$.
The $5\%$ size corrected weak instrument test $H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff
\mu^{2}\le10$ versus $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$ is $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$,
i.e. $c$ is the $95\%$ quantile of $\chi_{1}^{2}(10)$.  That is the
conventional Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical value

$c_{SY,10\%}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi_{1}^{2}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx
16\!-\!17$,

the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct, the $F\approx16$
value normally quoted in the tables.  The $\approx23$ value above is
the literal $95\%$ one-sided lower confidence bound for the
concentration parameter $\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ and
hence $R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$ with $95\%$ nominal coverage,
the $F\approx10$ mean rule inflated by the sampling uncertainty in
the first stage $F$. ∎
public_text.11:
Under the homoskedastic Nagar first order approximation with $k_{2}=1$

$R(\mu^{2})\simeq {\rm RelBias}_{2SLS/OLS}\simeq k_{2}/\mu^{2}\simeq1/\mu^{2}$,
$E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ and in the weak instrument limit

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})=\bigl[Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}\bigr]^{2}$,
$\qquad \sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1)$.

Hence $ \sqrt{\mu^{2}}\approx\sqrt{F_{1}}-Z$ and a $1-\alpha$ one sided
lower confidence bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ from an observed $f$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)\approx\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu^{2}_{L}(f)\approx\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{2}$,
$R_{U}(f)\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

The Nagar $10\%$ boundary is $R_{0}=0.10\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$.
Requiring $R_{U}<R_{0}$ i.e. $\mu_{L}^{2}\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ is

$\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}\iff
\sqrt{f^{*}}\;=\;\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

i.e. on the $\sqrt F$ normalisation

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Bigl[\sqrt{10}+z_{1-\alpha}\Bigr]^{2}$.

With the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\bigl[\sqrt{10}+1.645\bigr]^{2}
      \approx[3.162+1.645]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1$,

$F-1\approx22$, so that $F\gtrsim22\!-\!24$ gives a $95\%$ one sided
lower bound $\mu_{L}^{2}>10$ and hence $R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$
on the Nagar first order scale.  With the conventional two sided
$z_{0.975}=1.96$ this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$, the usual
$22\!-\!26$ $95\%$ confidence interval statement of the familiar
$F\approx10$ mean bias rule.

Remark.  On the usual Stock-Yogo $5\%$ size test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$, $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, the
$1-\alpha$ quantile of $F_{1,\infty}(10)$ is the $95^{\rm th}$ percentile
of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,

$c_{SY,10\%}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,

the $F\approx16$ value normally quoted in the tables as the $5\%$
size corrected $10\%$ maximal relative Nagar bias critical value, i.e.
the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct.  The $ \approx23$
figure above is the strict $95\%$ one sided lower confidence bound for
$\mu^{2}$ itself, $\mu_{L}^{2}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$, which is the
$F\approx10$ point rule inflated for the sampling error in the first
stage $F$. ∎
public_text.1:
In the homoskedastic just identified case $k_{2}=1$

${\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]\approx 
\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{v}^{-2} \mu^{-2}$ ,  
${\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]=\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{v}^{-2}$,

so that on Nagar first order

$R(\mu^{2})\equiv
{\rm Bias}_{2SLS}/{\rm Bias}_{OLS}\approx k_{2}\mu^{-2}
\approx\mu^{-2}\approx\big(EF-1\big)^{-1}\approx F^{-1}$,

$E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ and in the weak instrument limit
$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$ i.e.

$\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1)$, $Z\sim N(0,1)$.

Hence on the $\sqrt F$ scale

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,

and on the Nagar scale

$R_{U}(f)\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)
          \approx\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{-2}$.

The point Nagar $10\%$ boundary is
$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e. $\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$,
$\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx3.162$.
$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ iff

$\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

i.e. on the normal $\sqrt F$ approximation

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}=\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}$.

With the one-sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
       \approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}
       \approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1$,
$ f^{*}_{0.95}-1\approx22$,

so that $\mu^{2}_{L}=[\sqrt f-1.645]^{2}>10$ and hence
$R_{U}\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$ with $95\%$ one-sided confidence.
With the usual two-sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation this is
$[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$, the familiar $22\!-\!26$ range.
In the $1/F$ mean-bias shorthand this is the $F\approx10\!-\!11$ 
Nagar point rule lifted to the $95\%$ lower confidence bound for
$\mu^{2}$.

Remark.  On the conventional size-corrected Stock–Yogo test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$ the $5\%$ critical value is
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, i.e. the $95\%$ quantile of 
$\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$.  That is
$c_{SY}(k_{2}=1,10\%)\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$, the
$F\gtrsim16$ table value normally quoted as the $10\%$ maximal
relative Nagar bias rule, the $F>10$ mean-bias rule made $5\%$ size
correct. The $ \approx23$ number above is the literal $95\%$ one-sided
lower confidence bound $\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the
concentration parameter, i.e. the $F\approx10$ point rule inflated by
the sampling error in the first stage $F$.
public_text.18:
For the homoscedastic just identified model with $k_{2}=1$

${\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]\approx 
\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{v}^{-2}k_{2}\mu^{-2}$ , 
${\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]=\sigma_{uv}\sigma_{v}^{-2}$,

$R(\mu^{2})\equiv {\rm RelBias}\approx k_{2}\mu^{-2}\approx\mu^{-2}$,
$ {\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ , $F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$.

In weak instrument asymptotics

$F_{1}\approx\bigl(Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}\bigr)^{2}$ , $Z\sim N(0,1)$,
$\sqrt{F_{1}}\approx\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z$ ,
i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\sim N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ to first order.

Put $R_{0}=0.10$.  On the Nagar scale $R_{0}=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}$,

$\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$, $\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx3.16$.

For an observed $f$ a one-sided $1-\alpha$ lower bound for
$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}\simeq\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$.

Hence a $1-\alpha$ upper bound for the Nagar relative bias is

$R_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}\simeq\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{-2}$.

$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e.

$\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

$\;f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}\;.$

With the one-sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Big]^{2}
       \approx(3.162+1.645)^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx 23.1$ .

That is $F-1\approx22$, $F\approx 22\!-\!24$ on the
$\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ normalisation, $ \approx 26$
with the conventional two-sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$.  In the point mean
Nagar shorthand $R\simeq1/F$ this is the familiar $F\approx10\!-\!11$
rule lifted to a $95\%$ lower confidence bound for the concentration
parameter.

On the usual Stock–Yogo size-corrected test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$ the $5\%$ critical value is the
$0.95$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, $c_{SY}\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,

i.e. the conventional $F\gtrsim16$ $10\%$ maximal relative bias
reference, the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct.  The
$ \approx23$ value above is the literal $95\%$ one-sided lower
confidence bound $\mu_{L}^{2}=[\sqrt F-z_{0.95}]^{2}\ge10$ for the
concentration parameter, $\approx16.4$ on the Stock–Yogo $5\%$ size
calibration. ∎
public_text.15:
With $k_{2}=1$ the homoskedastic Nagar first order relative bias is

${\rm RelBias}_{N}\simeq \frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}}\simeq \mu^{-2}$ ,
${\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ ,
$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$ .

In weak instrument asymptotics

$\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\qquad Z\sim N(0,1)$,
i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$.

On a point estimate
${\rm RelBias}_{N}\approx1/F_{1}$ and
${\rm RelBias}_{N}=0.10\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/0.10=10$,
${\rm E}F_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}=11$, the familiar $F\approx10$ mean-bias rule.

For an observed $f$ a $1-\alpha$ one-sided lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$
on the $\sqrt F$ normal scale is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$ ,
so that on the Nagar scale

${\rm RelBias}_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)=\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{-2}$ .

${\rm RelBias}_{U}(f)\le0.10$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge10$ i.e.

$\sqrt f\ge \sqrt{10}+z_{1-\alpha}$ .

Hence the $1-\alpha$ lower confidence inversion on the $\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$
limit is

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2},
\qquad \mu_{0}^{2}=10.$

With the usual one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
      \approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}
      \approx4.81^{2}\approx 23.1$,

i.e. $f-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, 
$F\gtrsim22\!-\!24$ in round numbers.  With the conventional two sided
$z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$.

This is the literal $95\%$ one-sided lower confidence bound
$\mu_{L}^{2}=[\sqrt F-z_{0.95}]^{2}>10$ for the Nagar concentration
parameter, i.e. the $1/F$ rule $F\approx10$ lifted to a $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$.  In the conventional size-controlled
Stock–Yogo testing form $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$ the $5\%$ size
critical value is the $95\%$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,

$c_{SY,10\%,k=1}=q_{0.95}\!\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\big]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17,$

the $F>10$ mean bias rule made $5\%$ size correct and the value quoted
in practice as the $10\%$ maximal relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias threshold.
The $ \approx23$ figure above is the normal $\sqrt F$ $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself, the $ \approx16.4$ figure the
usual Stock–Yogo $5\%$ size corrected critical value. ∎
public_text.4:
For a just identified homoskedastic first stage the Nagar first order
relative bias is

${\rm RelBias}\equiv 
\frac{E[\hat \beta_{2SLS}-\beta]}{{\rm plim}[\hat \beta_{OLS}-\beta]}
\approx \frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}},\qquad k_{2}=1$,

and in the weak instrument limit with $\nu_{2}\to\infty$

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2}),\qquad 
\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1)$,

so that $E[F_{1}]=1+\mu^{2}$ and on the mean scale
${\rm RelBias}\approx\mu^{-2}\approx(F_{1}-1)^{-1}\approx F_{1}^{-1}$.
The point Nagar $10\%$ bias boundary is

$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}\iff \mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10,$
$E[F_{1}]_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}\approx 11$,

the familiar $F\approx10$ mean-bias rule.

Let $f$ be the observed first stage.  On the $\sqrt F$ normalisation

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}\approx \sqrt f -Z$,

so that a one sided $1-\alpha$ lower confidence bound for
$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ is

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)\approx\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu^{2}_{L}(f)\approx\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{2}$,
and

$R_{U}(f)\approx \mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e.

$\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}$,
$\sqrt{f^{*}}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$.

Hence on the $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ normal approximation

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\approx\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}$.

With $\mu_{0}^{2}=10$ and the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile
$z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\Big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Big]^{2}
\approx\bigl[3.162+1.645\bigr]^{2}
\approx4.81^{2}\approx 23\,{\rm -}\,24$,

$ f^{*}-1\approx22$, i.e. $F-1>10$ with $95\%$ one sided lower
confidence for $\mu^{2}$.  With the usual two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$
this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$, the $22\!-\!26$ range
usually quoted for the literal $95\%$ lower confidence bound
$\mu^{2}_{L}>10\iff R_{U}<0.10$.  The point mean rule is
$R\approx 1/F<0.10\iff F\approx10\!-\!11$.

Remark.  In test form the $5\%$ size weak instrument test of
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$ is
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, i.e. $c$ is the $95\%$ quantile of
$\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$.  The Stock–Yogo size corrected critical value is

$c_{SY,10\%}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38
\approx16\!-\!17$,

the $F\approx16$ value normally quoted in the literature as the
$95\%$ size/$10\%$ maximal relative Nagar bias threshold, the
$F>10$ point rule lifted to the conventional $5\%$ size calibration.
This is the $F\approx16.4$ Stock–Yogo table value that is used in
practice, the normal $\sqrt F$ inversion above being the
conservative $95\%$ lower confidence bound $\approx23$ for the
concentration parameter itself. ∎

${\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]\approx \sigma_{uv}\sigma_{vv}^{-1}\mu^{-2}$,

 \sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1),$

boundary

$R_{0}=0.10\iff \mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10 ,$

Requiring $R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ i.e. $\mu_{L}^{2}\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ gives the
normal inversion

$\sqrt{f^{*}}=\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{2}$.

With the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
\approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1$,

i.e. $F-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, $F\gtrsim
22\!-\!24$ on the $\sqrt{F}\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ weak instrument
normalisation.  With the conventional two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ this
is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$.  On the $F-1$ mean correction
$\sqrt{F-1}\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ this is $F^{*}\approx
\big[\sqrt{10}+z_{0.95}\big]^{2}+1\approx24$, the usual $F\approx
23\!-\!26$ $95\%$ one sided lower confidence bound for the
concentration parameter, i.e. the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule lifted
to a $95\%$ lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$.

In particular the point Nagar mean requirement is $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff

test

$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$,

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}\!\left[F>c\right]=0.05,$

is the Stock–Yogo $5\%$ size test.  On the non-central limit
$F\mid\mu^{2}=10\to\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$

$c_{0.05}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx
16\!-\!17$,

the familiar Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical value
for $k_{2}=1$, the $F>10$ mean rule made $5\%$ size correct.  This is
the $F\approx16$ value normally quoted in applied work, the $23$
value above being the strict $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ $95\%$
lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself. ∎

18.text:
For a just–identified homoscedastic model with $k_{2}=1$,
\begin{equation*}
R(\mu^{2})\equiv
\frac{{\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]}{{\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]}
\;\approx\;\frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}}\approx\frac{1}{\mu^{2}},\qquad 
{\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2} .
\end{equation*}
On the weak–instrument limit
\begin{equation*}
F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2}),\qquad 
\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1) ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N\!\left(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1\right)$.
Hence a one–sided $1-\alpha$ lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ from an
observed $f$ is
\begin{equation*}
\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha},\qquad
\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{2},
\end{equation*}
and $R_{U}(f)\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

The Nagar $10\%$ boundary is
$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e. $\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$.
$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e.
\begin{equation*}
\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha},\qquad
f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\approx\Bigl[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Bigr]^{2}.
\end{equation*}
With the one–sided 95$\,\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,
\begin{equation*}
f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\Bigl[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Bigr]^{2}
           \approx(3.162+1.645)^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $F-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, $F\approx
22\!-\!24$, about $F\approx23$ on the $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$
weak instrument normalisation, $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$ on the
conventional two–sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation.  In the point
mean Nagar shorthand $R\simeq1/F$ this is the familiar $F\approx10\!-\!11$
rule, $EF_{0}\approx11$, lifted to the $95\%$ lower confidence bound
$\mu_{L}^{2}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the concentration parameter.

Remark.  On the conventional size–controlled weak–instrument test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$, $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, the $5\%$
critical value is the $95\%$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,
\begin{equation*}
c_{SY,10\%}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17,
\end{equation*}
the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias critical value
normally quoted as the $F\gtrsim16$ weak–instrument rule, the $F>10$
point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct.  This is the $F\approx16$
operative Stock–Yogo table value that is usually reported as “$95\%$
confident, in the size–corrected sense, that the Nagar relative bias is
$<10\%$”, the $\approx23$ figure above being the strict
$\sqrt F-z$ $95\%$ one–sided lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself.

Weak instrument limit F1→d χ²1(μ²)=[Z+√μ²]², √F1≈√μ²+Z, Z∼N(0,1). On the √F normalisation a 1-α one-sided lower bound for √μ² is √μ²L≈√f−z1-α and the usual normal delta inversion for a Nagar 10% bound is

√f* = √μ0²+z1-α ,   f*=[√10+z1-α]² .

With z0.95=1.645 this is f*≈(3.162+1.645)²≈23.1, f*−1≈22, ≈26.2 with z0.975=1.96. That is the literal 95% one-sided lower confidence bound μL²=(√F−z)²>10 ⇒ RelBiasU≈μL⁻²<0.10 on the √F≈N(√μ²,1) delta method. This is the ≈22-26 conservative normal lower-bound that is repeatedly quoted in the round.

The operational weak-instrument test used in practice is the size-controlled Stock–Yogo test

H0: RelBias≥0.10 ⇔ μ²≤10 vs H1: μ²>10,

reject H0 at 5% when Pμ²=10[F>c]=0.05. With ν2→∞ F1→d χ²1(μ²) so c is the 0.95 quantile of χ²1(10). Numerically

cSY = q0.95[χ²1(10)]≈16.38≈16-17,

the conventional 10% maximal relative 2SLS/OLS bias critical value for k2=1, often quoted as F≳16. This is the 5% size-corrected version of the F≈10 point Nagar rule and is the value most colleagues now cite as the “95% confident” weak instrument threshold.

Hence the discussion remains the test-size vs confidence-bound interpretation. The Stock–Yogo size-corrected inversion gives ≈16, the nearest whole number 16, essentially the F>10 rule made 5% size correct. The strict √F normal delta lower confidence bound for μ² itself gives ≈23, ≈26 two-sided, the conservative normal-approximation bound for RelBiasU<0.10 with 95% nominal coverage. reflection_text.18:
For a just–identified homoscedastic model with $k_{2}=1$,
\begin{equation*}
R(\mu^{2})\equiv
\frac{{\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]}{{\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]}
\;\approx\;\frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}}\approx\frac{1}{\mu^{2}},\qquad 
{\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2} .
\end{equation*}
On the weak–instrument limit
\begin{equation*}
F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2}),\qquad 
\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1) ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N\!\left(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1\right)$.
Hence a one–sided $1-\alpha$ lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$ from an
observed $f$ is
\begin{equation*}
\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha},\qquad
\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{2},
\end{equation*}
and $R_{U}(f)\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

The Nagar $10\%$ boundary is
$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e. $\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$.
$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$, i.e.
\begin{equation*}
\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha},\qquad
f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\approx\Bigl[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Bigr]^{2}.
\end{equation*}
With the one–sided 95$\,\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,
\begin{equation*}
f^{*}_{0.95}\approx\Bigl[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Bigr]^{2}
           \approx(3.162+1.645)^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $F-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, $F\approx
22\!-\!24$, about $F\approx23$ on the $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$
weak instrument normalisation, $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$ on the
conventional two–sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation.  In the point
mean Nagar shorthand $R\simeq1/F$ this is the familiar $F\approx10\!-\!11$
rule, $EF_{0}\approx11$, lifted to the $95\%$ lower confidence bound
$\mu_{L}^{2}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the concentration parameter.

Remark.  On the conventional size–controlled weak–instrument test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$, $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, the $5\%$
critical value is the $95\%$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,
\begin{equation*}
c_{SY,10\%}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17,
\end{equation*}
the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias critical value
normally quoted as the $F\gtrsim16$ weak–instrument rule, the $F>10$
point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct.  This is the $F\approx16$
operative Stock–Yogo table value that is usually reported as “$95\%$
confident, in the size–corrected sense, that the Nagar relative bias is
$<10\%$”, the $\approx23$ figure above being the strict
$\sqrt F-z$ $95\%$ one–sided lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With $k_{2}=1$ the homoskedastic Nagar first order is

${\rm RelBias}_{N}\simeq k_{2}/\mu^{2}\simeq 1/(E F-1)\simeq 1/F$,    $E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$.

The point $10\%$ rule is $\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/0.10=10$, i.e. $E F_{0}=11$, the familiar $F\approx10$ mean bias rule.

The statement that is actually used as “$95\%$ confident that the Nagar relative asymptotic bias is $<10\%$” is the size-controlled weak instrument test

$H_{0}: R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le\mu_{0}^{2}=10$  vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$,

rejected at $5\%$ size when $F_{1}$ exceeds the $95\%$ quantile of the first stage under the boundary $\mu^{2}=10$.

In the weak instrument limit $\nu_{2}\to\infty$

$F_{1}\to_{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$,   $F_{1}\approx[Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}]^{2}$,

so

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F_{1}>c]=0.05\iff P_{\chi^{2}_{1}(10)}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)>c]=0.05$.

That is the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias $5\%$ size critical value for $L=1$,

$c_{0.10}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx 16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,

the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct.  An observed $F>c_{0.10}$ rejects $\mu^{2}\le10$ at the conventional $5\%$ level, i.e. in the operational weak-instrument sense we can say with $95\%$ confidence that the Nagar asymptotic relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias is $<10\%$.

The $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ inversion $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}=\sqrt F-z_{0.95}$ and the requirement $\mu^{2}_{L}\ge10$, i.e. $\sqrt f^{*}= \sqrt{10}+z_{0.95}$ and $f^{*}\approx[\sqrt{10}+1.645]^{2}\approx23.1$, is a $95\%$ lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter itself, $\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z)^{2}>10$, and then a point transformation $R\approx1/\mu^{2}$. It is a Bonferroni-type bound on $\mu^{2}$ and double counts sampling variation: the first stage $F$ is already the test statistic for $\mu^{2}$. The proper size control is $P(F>c|\mu^{2}=10)=0.05$, not $\mu^{2}_{L}\ge10$.

Hence on the Nagar/Stock–Yogo calibration that is used in practice the $10\%$ maximal relative bias threshold for one instrument is the size-corrected value $q_{0.95}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)]\approx16.4$, conventionally quoted as $F\gtrsim16$, essentially $F\approx16$ in round numbers. That is the textbook $F>10$ mean rule lifted to its $5\%$ weak instrument size-corrected form.

$\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{2}$,
$R_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

The Nagar $10\%$ point is

$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$,
$\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx3.162$,
$EF_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}\simeq11$, the familiar $F\approx10$ mean bias rule.

$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ i.e.

$\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}\iff
\sqrt{f^{*}}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

so on the $\sqrt F$ normalisation

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}$.

With the one sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
\approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1,$

i.e. $f^{*}-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation.  Hence
$\mu_{L}^{2}=[\sqrt F-1.645]^{2}>10$ and $R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$
with $95\%$ one sided nominal coverage.  With the conventional two
sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$, the
usual $22\!-\!26$ $95\%$ lower confidence range for the concentration
parameter, the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule lifted to a $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$.

$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff\mu^{2}\le10$, $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$, the $5\%$
critical value is the $0.95$ quantile of $\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$,

$c_{SY}=q_{0.95}\!\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\big]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17,$

the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative Nagar bias critical value for
$k_{2}=1$, i.e. the $F>10$ point rule made $5\%$ size correct and the
value normally quoted in the tables as $F\gtrsim16$.  The $\approx23$
figure above is the literal $95\%$ one sided lower confidence bound
$\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the concentration parameter
itself.

With $k_{2}=1$ the homoskedastic Nagar first order is

${\rm RelBias}_{N}\simeq k_{2}/\mu^{2}\simeq 1/(E F-1)\simeq 1/F$,    $E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$.

The point $10\%$ rule is $\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/0.10=10$, i.e. $E F_{0}=11$, the familiar $F\approx10$ mean bias rule.

The statement that is actually used as “$95\%$ confident that the Nagar relative asymptotic bias is $<10\%$” is the size-controlled weak instrument test

$H_{0}: R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le\mu_{0}^{2}=10$  vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$,

rejected at $5\%$ size when $F_{1}$ exceeds the $95\%$ quantile of the first stage under the boundary $\mu^{2}=10$.

In the weak instrument limit $\nu_{2}\to\infty$

$F_{1}\to_{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$,   $F_{1}\approx[Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}]^{2}$,

so

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F_{1}>c]=0.05\iff P_{\chi^{2}_{1}(10)}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)>c]=0.05$.

That is the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias $5\%$ size critical value for $L=1$,

$c_{0.10}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx 16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,

the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct.  An observed $F>c_{0.10}$ rejects $\mu^{2}\le10$ at the conventional $5\%$ level, i.e. in the operational weak-instrument sense we can say with $95\%$ confidence that the Nagar asymptotic relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias is $<10\%$.

The $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ inversion $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}=\sqrt F-z_{0.95}$ and the requirement $\mu^{2}_{L}\ge10$, i.e. $\sqrt f^{*}= \sqrt{10}+z_{0.95}$ and $f^{*}\approx[\sqrt{10}+1.645]^{2}\approx23.1$, is a $95\%$ lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter itself, $\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z)^{2}>10$, and then a point transformation $R\approx1/\mu^{2}$. It is a Bonferroni-type bound on $\mu^{2}$ and double counts sampling variation: the first stage $F$ is already the test statistic for $\mu^{2}$. The proper size control is $P(F>c|\mu^{2}=10)=0.05$, not $\mu^{2}_{L}\ge10$.

Hence on the Nagar/Stock–Yogo calibration that is used in practice the $10\%$ maximal relative bias threshold for one instrument is the size-corrected value $q_{0.95}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)]\approx16.4$, conventionally quoted as $F\gtrsim16$, essentially $F\approx16$ in round numbers. That is the textbook $F>10$ mean rule lifted to its $5\%$ weak instrument size-corrected form.

The Nagar first-order relative bias for the just identified homoskedastic case is

RelBias ≃ k2/μ² , k2=1,   E[F1]=1+μ² ,   RelBias ≃1/(F-1)≃1/F

on the mean.  The point 10% boundary is μ0² = k2/0.10 =10, i.e. E[F]≈11, the familiar F≈10 mean-bias rule.

The operational “95% confident that RelBias<0.10” used in the weak-instrument literature is the size-corrected Stock–Yogo test

H0 : RelBias ≥0.10 ⇔ H0 : μ² ≤ μ0² =10   vs   H1 : μ²>10,

rejected at 5% size when F1 exceeds the 95% quantile of the first stage under the boundary μ²=10.  In the ν2→∞ limit

F1 →d χ²1(μ²) = [Z+√μ²]² ,   Z∼N(0,1),

so the 5% critical value solves

P_{μ²=10}[F1>c]=0.05 ⇔ P_{μ²=10}[χ²1(10)>c]=0.05.

That is the 95th percentile of a non-central χ²1 with non-centrality 10, i.e. the 95th percentile of F1,∞(10). Numerically

c0.10 = q0.95[χ²1(10)] ≈ 16.38 ≈ 16–17,

the published Stock–Yogo 10% maximal relative bias critical value for L=1.  An observed F>c rejects μ²≤10 at the conventional 5% level, which is the conventional operational meaning of “with 95% confidence the Nagar asymptotic relative bias is <10%”.

The √F≈N(√μ²,1) inversion √μ²L = √F−z0.95 and the requirement μ²L≥10 gives √f* =√10+z0.95 and f*≈(√10+1.645)²≈23.1. The first-stage F is already the test statistic for μ²; E[F]=1+μ² already incorporates the sampling error of the first stage. Imposing μ²L=(√F−z)²≥10 double counts that sampling variation.

Hence on the Nagar/Stock–Yogo calibration that is actually used in practice the 10% maximal relative bias threshold for one instrument is the 5% size-corrected value

F*≈q0.95[χ²1(10)]≈16.4,

conventionally quoted as F≳16.  That is the F>10 mean Nagar rule lifted to the usual 5% weak-instrument size. The ≈23 figure is the conservative normal-approximation lower confidence bound for μ² itself, not the conventional size-corrected Stock–Yogo critical value for H0:R≥0.10.

With $k_{2}=1$ and i.i.d. homoskedastic errors the Nagar first order
relative bias is

${\rm RelBias}_{N}(\mu^{2})\simeq 
\frac{{\rm E}[\hat\beta_{2SLS}-\beta]}{{\rm plim}[\hat\beta_{OLS}-\beta]}
\simeq\frac{k_{2}}{\mu^{2}}\simeq\frac1{EF_{1}-1}\simeq\frac1{F_{1}}$

and in the weak instrument limit with $\nu_{2}\to\infty$

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi_{1}^{2}(\mu^{2}),\qquad 
\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\;Z\sim N(0,1),$

so that on the $\sqrt F$ scale

$\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N\!\left(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1\right),\qquad 
E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}.$

For an observed $f$ a $1-\alpha$ one-sided lower bound for $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}$
is therefore

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha},\qquad 
\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{2},$

and on the Nagar scale

$R_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

The $10\%$ Nagar point is

$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10,
\qquad\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx3.162.$

$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ i.e.

$\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}\iff
\sqrt{f^{*}}=\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha},$

i.e. on the $\sqrt F$ normal weak-instrument approximation

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2},
\qquad\mu_{0}^{2}=10.$

With the one-sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Big]^{2}\approx
[3.162+1.645]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1,$

i.e. $f^{*}-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation,
$F\gtrsim 22$–$24$ on the usual $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$
approximation.  In particular

$\mu_{L}^{2}=[\sqrt F-1.645]^{2}>10\Longleftrightarrow 
R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$

with $95\%$ one-sided nominal coverage.  With the conventional
two-sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ normalisation this is
$[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$, the familiar $22\!-\!26$ $95\%$
lower confidence range for the concentration parameter.  On the
point mean Nagar scale this is the familiar $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff
F\gtrsim10\!-\!11$, $EF_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}=11$, lifted to a
$95\%$ lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$.

Remark on the usual size-corrected usage.  In testing form
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le10$ is rejected at $5\%$ size when
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$.  With $\nu_{2}\to\infty$
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=P\big[\chi_{1}^{2}(10)>c\big]=0.05$, i.e. $c$
is the $95\%$ quantile of $\chi_{1}^{2}(10)$,

$c_{SY,10\%}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi_{1}^{2}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx
16\!-\!17,$

the published Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical value
for $k_{2}=1$.  This is the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size
correct and is the $F\gtrsim16$ value conventionally quoted in the
weak-instrument tables as the operational “$95\%$ confident, $10\%$
maximal relative bias’’ threshold.  The $\approx23$ figure above is the
strict $95\%$ one-sided lower confidence bound
$\mu_{L}^{2}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the concentration parameter
itself, i.e. the literal confidence inversion of the Nagar bias. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The just-identified homoscedastic Nagar first order is
${\rm RelBias}_{N}\simeq k_{2}\mu^{-2}$ with $k_{2}=1$, $E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ and
in the weak instrument limit $F_{1}\to_{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$, i.e.
$\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1)$, $Z\sim N(0,1)$, so
$\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel a\sim N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$.
On the mean scale $R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}$ gives $\mu_{0}^{2}=10$,
$\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}\simeq3.162$, $EF_{0}\simeq11$, the familiar $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff F\gtrsim10\!-\!11$ point Nagar rule.

For an observed $f$ the $1-\alpha$ one sided lower bound on the $\sqrt F$
scale is $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}]^{2}$ and $R_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.
$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ i.e.
$\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$ and
$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}]^{2}$.

With the one-sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,
$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq[\sqrt{10}+1.645]^{2}\approx[4.807]^{2}\approx23.1$,
i.e. $f^{*}-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, $F\gtrsim22\!-\!24$
on the $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ weak instrument normalisation.
With the conventional two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$.
Hence $\mu^{2}_{L}=[\sqrt F-1.645]^{2}>10$ gives $R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$
with $95\%$ one sided nominal coverage; the strict $\sqrt F-z$ lower confidence
bound for the concentration parameter is the $\approx 23\!-\!26$ range, often quoted
as $\approx23$.

This is distinct from the operational size-corrected weak instrument test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le10$ vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$,
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$.  With $\nu_{2}\to\infty$ $F_{1}\mid\mu^{2}=10\to
\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$, so the $5\%$ size critical value is
$c_{SY}=q_{0.95}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,
the published Stock-Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical value for
$L=1$.  $F>c_{SY}$ rejects $\mu^{2}\le10$ at $5\%$ and is the value normally
quoted in practice as “$95\%$ confident / $5\%$ size that $R<0.10$”, i.e.
the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct, conventionally $F\gtrsim16$.

The deliberation shows a persistent split: a literal $95\%$ lower confidence
bound for $\mu^{2}$ via the $\sqrt F$ normal approximation gives $\approx
23\!-\!26$, about $23$ one sided, whereas the conventional Stock-Yogo size
corrected calibration that is actually tabulated is $\approx16.4$, often
rounded to $16\!-\!17$, with some normal-delta approximations giving
$\approx20\!-\!21$ for $F-z\sqrt{2F}=10$.  The $F\approx10$ mean bias rule,
the $\approx16$ Stock-Yogo $5\%$ size rule and the $\approx23$ strict
$\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z)^{2}>10$ lower confidence bound are all being used
interchangeably in the discussion, with the $16$ value being the operational
weak instrument threshold and the $23$ value being the literal $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for the concentration parameter and hence for the Nagar
relative bias.

The just-identified homoscedastic Nagar first order relative bias is
R ≃ k2/μ², k2=1, with E[F]=1+μ² and in the weak instrument limit
F1 →d χ²1(μ²), √F1 ≃ √μ²+Z, Z∼N(0,1). On the mean scale R≃1/μ²≃1/(F-1)≃1/F
and the point 10% boundary is μ0²=k2/0.10=10, EF0≈11, the familiar F≈10-11 rule.

Sampling variation matters. On the √F normalisation √μ²≈√F−Z, so a 1−α one-sided lower bound for √μ² from an observed f is √μ²L=√f−z1−α and μ²L=[√f−z1−α]². The Nagar upper bound for the relative bias is RU≈μL⁻². Requiring RU≤0.10 i.e. μL²≥10 gives √f≥√μ0²+z1−α and the inversion f*1−α=[√μ0²+z1−α]² with μ0²=10.

With the one-sided 95% normal quantile z0.95=1.645
f*0.95≈[√10+1.645]²≈[3.162+1.645]²≈4.81²≈23.1, i.e. F−1≈22, about 22-24 on the √F≈N(√μ²,1) weak-instrument approximation, ≈26.2 with the conventional two-sided z0.975=1.96. This is the literal 95% one-sided lower confidence bound for μ², μL²=(√F−z)²>10 ⇒ RU≈1/μL²<0.10.

The literature operationalises the same statement as the size-corrected Stock–Yogo weak-instrument test H0:R≥0.10 ⇔ μ²≤10 rejected at 5% size when Pμ²=10[F>c]=0.05. With ν2→∞ F|μ²=10→d χ²1(10) and cSY,10%,k=1 = q0.95[χ²1(10)]≈16.38≈16-17, the conventional F≳16 table value, the F>10 mean-bias rule made 5% size correct.

The just-identified homoscedastic Nagar first order is
${\rm RelBias}_{N}\simeq k_{2}\mu^{-2}$ with $k_{2}=1$, $E F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$ and
in the weak instrument limit $F_{1}\to_{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$, i.e.
$\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1)$, $Z\sim N(0,1)$, so
$\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel a\sim N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$.
On the mean scale $R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}$ gives $\mu_{0}^{2}=10$,
$\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}\simeq3.162$, $EF_{0}\simeq11$, the familiar $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff F\gtrsim10\!-\!11$ point Nagar rule.

For an observed $f$ the $1-\alpha$ one sided lower bound on the $\sqrt F$
scale is $\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}]^{2}$ and $R_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.
$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ i.e.
$\sqrt f\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$ and
$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}]^{2}$.

With the one-sided $95\%$ normal quantile $z_{0.95}=1.645$,
$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq[\sqrt{10}+1.645]^{2}\approx[4.807]^{2}\approx23.1$,
i.e. $f^{*}-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ normalisation, $F\gtrsim22\!-\!24$
on the $\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ weak instrument normalisation.
With the conventional two sided $z_{0.975}=1.96$ this is $[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$.
Hence $\mu^{2}_{L}=[\sqrt F-1.645]^{2}>10$ gives $R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$
with $95\%$ one sided nominal coverage; the strict $\sqrt F-z$ lower confidence
bound for the concentration parameter is the $\approx 23\!-\!26$ range, often quoted
as $\approx23$.

This is distinct from the operational size-corrected weak instrument test
$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le10$ vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$,
$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$.  With $\nu_{2}\to\infty$ $F_{1}\mid\mu^{2}=10\to
\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$, so the $5\%$ size critical value is
$c_{SY}=q_{0.95}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,
the published Stock-Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias critical value for
$L=1$.  $F>c_{SY}$ rejects $\mu^{2}\le10$ at $5\%$ and is the value normally
quoted in practice as “$95\%$ confident / $5\%$ size that $R<0.10$”, i.e.
the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct, conventionally $F\gtrsim16$.

The deliberation shows a persistent split: a literal $95\%$ lower confidence
bound for $\mu^{2}$ via the $\sqrt F$ normal approximation gives $\approx
23\!-\!26$, about $23$ one sided, whereas the conventional Stock-Yogo size
corrected calibration that is actually tabulated is $\approx16.4$, often
rounded to $16\!-\!17$, with some normal-delta approximations giving
$\approx20\!-\!21$ for $F-z\sqrt{2F}=10$.  The $F\approx10$ mean bias rule,
the $\approx16$ Stock-Yogo $5\%$ size rule and the $\approx23$ strict
$\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z)^{2}>10$ lower confidence bound are all being used
interchangeably in the discussion, with the $16$ value being the operational
weak instrument threshold and the $23$ value being the literal $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for the concentration parameter and hence for the Nagar
relative bias.

$R(\mu^{2})\simeq k_{2}\mu^{-2}\simeq\mu^{-2}\simeq (EF_{1}-1)^{-1}\simeq F_{1}^{-1}$,
$EF_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$,

so on the mean $R_{0}=0.10\iff \mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$ and $EF_{0}\approx11$,
the familiar $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule.

The operational “95% confident that the asymptotic relative bias is $<10\%$’’ in the weak instrument literature is the size controlled test

$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le\mu_{0}^{2}=10$ vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$,

rejected at $5\%$ size when $F_{1}>c$ with

In the $\nu_{2}\to\infty$ weak instrument limit

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})=[Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}]^{2}$,

so under the boundary

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F_{1}>c]=P\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)>c\big]=0.05$.

Hence $c$ is the $95\%$ quantile of a non-central $\chi^{2}_{1}$ with non-centrality $10$, i.e. the $95\%$ quantile of $F_{1,\infty}(10)$. That is the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias $5\%$ size critical value for $L=1$.

$c_{0.10}=q_{0.95}\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\big]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$.

An observed $F>c$ rejects $\mu^{2}\le10$ at the conventional $5\%$ level, which is the usual textbook meaning of “with 95% confidence the Nagar asymptotic relative 2SLS/OLS bias is $<10\%$”. This is the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct, conventionally quoted as $F\gtrsim16$.

The $\sqrt{F}\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ inversion

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}=\sqrt{F}-z_{0.95},\qquad\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt{F}-z_{0.95})^{2}$,

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})=[Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}]^{2}$,
$\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1)$, $Z\sim N(0,1) $,

i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N\!\left(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1\right)$.
For an observed $f$

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=\big[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\big]^{2}$,
$R_{U}(f)\simeq \mu_{L}^{-2}(f)$.

The Nagar $10\%$ point on the mean is

$R_{0}=0.10=k_{2}/\mu_{0}^{2}\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$,
$\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx3.162$,
${\rm E}F_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}\approx11$,

the familiar $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff F\gtrsim10\!-\!11$ rule.
$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}\iff\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ i.e.

$\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}\iff
\sqrt{f^{*}_{1-\alpha}}=\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}$,

so on the $\sqrt F$ normalisation

$f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}$,
$\mu_{0}^{2}=10$.

One sided $95\%$ $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\big]^{2}
\approx\big[3.162+1.645\big]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1$,

i.e. $f^{*}-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ scale.  Hence

$\mu_{L}^{2}=[\sqrt F-1.645]^{2}>10\iff R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$

with $95\%$ one-sided nominal coverage.  With the conventional two
sided normalisation $z_{0.975}=1.96$

$f^{*}\simeq[\sqrt{10}+1.96]^{2}\approx26.2$,

the $22\!-\!26$ literal $95\%$ lower confidence bound for the
concentration parameter $\mu^{2}$ and hence for $R\simeq\mu^{-2}$.
This is the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule lifted to a $95\%$ lower
confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself. 

Remark on the operational testing convention.  The weak instrument
test that is used in practice is

$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le10$ vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$,
rejected at $5\%$ size when $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$.  With
$\nu_{2}\to\infty$, $F_{1}\mid\mu^{2}=10\to\chi^{2}_{1}(10)$ so that
the $5\%$ size critical value is

$c_{SY}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$,

the published Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative $2SLS/OLS$ bias
critical value for $L=1$, i.e. the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$
size correct and the $F\gtrsim16$ value normally quoted in the tables
as the $95\%$ confidence/$5\%$ size weak instrument threshold.  The
$\approx23$ $\approx26$ two-sided figure above is the strict
$\sqrt F-z$ $95\%$ lower confidence bound $\mu_{L}^{2}
=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the concentration parameter itself;
$c_{SY}\approx16.4$ is the conventional Stock–Yogo size-corrected
operational threshold. ∎

8.text:
With $k_{2}=1$ homoskedastic Nagar

${\rm RelBias}_{N}\simeq R(\mu^{2})\simeq \mu^{-2}$, 
$E\,F_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$, $R\simeq (EF-1)^{-1}\simeq F^{-1}$ on the mean,
and on the weak instrument limit $\nu_{2}\to\infty$

$$
F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})=\bigl[\,Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}\,\bigr]^{2},
\qquad Z\sim N(0,1),
$$

i.e.  

$$
\sqrt{F_{1}}=\sqrt{\mu^{2}}+Z+o_{p}(1),\qquad 
\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N\!\bigl(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1\bigr) .
$$

For an observed $f$

$$
\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}(f)=\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha},\qquad 
\mu^{2}_{L}(f)=\bigl[\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{2},
\qquad 
R_{U}(f)\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}(f) .
$$

The $10\%$ Nagar point is

$$
R_{0}=0.10=\frac{k_{2}}{\mu_{0}^{2}}\iff\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/0.10=10,
\qquad\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx 3.162,
\qquad EF_{0}=1+\mu_{0}^{2}\approx 11,
$$

the familiar $F\approx10\!-\!11$ mean bias rule $R\simeq1/F$.
$R_{U}(f)\le R_{0}$ iff $\mu_{L}^{2}(f)\ge\mu_{0}^{2}$ i.e.

$$
\sqrt f-z_{1-\alpha}\ge\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}},\qquad 
\sqrt{f^{*}_{1-\alpha}}=\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha},
$$

so on the $\sqrt F$ normalisation

$$
f^{*}_{1-\alpha}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{\mu_{0}^{2}}+z_{1-\alpha}\Big]^{2}.
$$

One sided $95\%$ $z_{0.95}=1.645$,

$$
f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\Big[\sqrt{10}+1.645\Big]^{2}
       \approx\bigl[3.162+1.645\bigr]^{2}
       \approx4.81^{2}\approx 23.1,
$$

i.e. $f^{*}-1\approx22$ on the $EF=1+\mu^{2}$ scale.  In particular

$$
\mu_{L}^{2}=\bigl[\sqrt F-1.645\bigr]^{2}>10\iff
R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10
$$

with $95\%$ one sided nominal coverage.  With the conventional two
sided normalisation $z_{0.975}=1.96$,

$$
f^{*}\simeq\bigl[\sqrt{10}+1.96\bigr]^{2}\approx26.2,
$$

the $22\!-\!26$ literal $95\%$ lower confidence bound for the
concentration parameter, the $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule lifted to a
$95\%$ lower confidence bound for $\mu^{2}$ itself.

Remark on the operational testing convention.  The size controlled
weak-instrument test normally quoted is

$$
H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le10\quad{\rm vs}\quad
H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10,
$$

rejected at $5\%$ size when $P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F>c]=0.05$.  With
$F_{1,\infty}\to\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$

$$
c_{SY}=q_{0.95}\!\left[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\right]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17,
$$

the published Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias $5\%$ size
critical value for $L=1$, i.e. the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$
size correct and the $F\gtrsim16$ value conventionally quoted in the
literature as the ``$95\%$ confident / $5\%$ size'' weak instrument
threshold.  The $\approx23$ number above is the strict
$\sqrt F\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ $95\%$ one sided lower confidence
bound $\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt F-z_{0.95})^{2}>10$ for the concentration
parameter itself, $R_{U}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$, the $\approx16.4$
number being the conventional Stock–Yogo size corrected $10\%$
maximal relative bias threshold. ∎

\qquad {\rm E}F_{1}=1+\mu^{2},$

i.e. $\sqrt{F_{1}}\stackrel{a}{\sim}N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$.  On the mean

the familiar $R\simeq1/F<0.10\iff F\gtrsim10\!-\!11$ Nagar point rule.

$\mu_{0}^{2}=10$.

$f^{*}_{0.95}\simeq\bigl[\sqrt{10}+1.645\bigr]^{2}
      \approx[3.162+1.645]^{2}\approx4.81^{2}\approx23.1,$

public_text.5:
With k2=1 the homoskedastic Nagar first order is 
R(μ²)≈k2/μ²≈μ⁻² and EF1=1+μ². On the mean scale the 10% point is 
R0=0.10⇔ μ0²=k2/R0=10, EF0≈11, the familiar F≈10 mean-bias rule.

The statement that is used in the weak-instrument literature as “95% confident that the asymptotic relative 2SLS/OLS bias is <10%’’ is the size-controlled test

H0 : R ≥0.10 ⇔ H0 : μ² ≤ μ0² =10   vs   H1 : μ²>10

rejected at 5% size when F1>c with 
P_{μ²=10}[F1>c]=0.05.

In the weak-instrument limit ν2→∞
F1 →d χ²1(μ²)=[Z+√μ²]², Z∼N(0,1),
so under the boundary

P_{μ²=10}[F1>c]=P[χ²1(10)>c]=0.05.

Hence c is the 95th percentile of a non-central χ²1 with non-centrality 10, i.e. the 95th percentile of F1,∞(10). That is the Stock–Yogo 10% maximal relative bias critical value for L=1.

c0.10 = q0.95[χ²1(10)] ≈16.38 ≈16–17.

An observed F>c rejects μ²≤10 at the conventional 5% level, which is the operational 95%/5% size meaning of 
“with 95% confidence the Nagar asymptotic relative bias is <10%’’.

The √F≈N(√μ²,1) inversion √μ²L=√F−z0.95, μ²L=(√F−z0.95)² and the requirement μ²L≥10, i.e. √f*=√10+z0.95 and f*≈[√10+1.645]²≈23.1, is a 95% lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter itself and then a point plug-in R≈1/μ²L. The first stage F is already the test statistic for μ², E[F]=1+μ² already incorporates its sampling error. Imposing μ²L=(√F−z)²≥10 double counts the sampling variation in F and is a Bonferroni-type bound on μ² followed by a point transformation.

The size-corrected calibration is P(F>c|μ²=10)=0.05 once, not μ²L≥10. That is the calibration Stock–Yogo tabulate and the value actually quoted in practice for the 10% maximal relative Nagar bias rule. In round numbers the textbook threshold for one instrument is F≳16.4, conventionally quoted as F≈16.
public_text.2:
With $k_{2}=1$ the homoskedastic Nagar first order is

$R(\mu^{2})\simeq k_{2}\mu^{-2}\simeq\mu^{-2}\simeq (EF_{1}-1)^{-1}\simeq F_{1}^{-1}$,
$EF_{1}=1+\mu^{2}$,

so on the mean $R_{0}=0.10\iff \mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/R_{0}=10$ and $EF_{0}\approx11$,
the familiar $F\approx10$ point Nagar rule.

The operational “95% confident that the asymptotic relative bias is $<10\%$’’ in the weak instrument literature is the size controlled test

$H_{0}:R\ge0.10\iff H_{0}:\mu^{2}\le\mu_{0}^{2}=10$ vs $H_{1}:\mu^{2}>10$,

rejected at $5\%$ size when $F_{1}>c$ with

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F_{1}>c]=0.05$.

In the $\nu_{2}\to\infty$ weak instrument limit

$F_{1}\xrightarrow{d}\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})=[Z+\sqrt{\mu^{2}}]^{2}$,

so under the boundary

$P_{\mu^{2}=10}[F_{1}>c]=P\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)>c\big]=0.05$.

Hence $c$ is the $95\%$ quantile of a non-central $\chi^{2}_{1}$ with non-centrality $10$, i.e. the $95\%$ quantile of $F_{1,\infty}(10)$. That is the Stock–Yogo $10\%$ maximal relative bias $5\%$ size critical value for $L=1$.

$c_{0.10}=q_{0.95}\big[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)\big]\approx16.38\approx16\!-\!17$.

An observed $F>c$ rejects $\mu^{2}\le10$ at the conventional $5\%$ level, which is the usual textbook meaning of “with 95% confidence the Nagar asymptotic relative 2SLS/OLS bias is $<10\%$”. This is the $F>10$ point Nagar rule made $5\%$ size correct, conventionally quoted as $F\gtrsim16$.

The $\sqrt{F}\approx N(\sqrt{\mu^{2}},1)$ inversion

$\sqrt{\mu^{2}}_{L}=\sqrt{F}-z_{0.95},\qquad\mu^{2}_{L}=(\sqrt{F}-z_{0.95})^{2}$,

and the requirement $\mu^{2}_{L}\ge10$, i.e. $\sqrt{f^{*}}=\sqrt{10}+z_{0.95}$ and $f^{*}\approx[\sqrt{10}+1.645]^{2}\approx23.1$, is a $95\%$ lower confidence bound for the concentration parameter $\mu^{2}$ itself and then a point map $R\approx1/\mu^{2}$. The first stage $F$ is already the test statistic for $\mu^{2}$; imposing $\mu^{2}_{L}\ge10$ on top of the sampling distribution of $F$ double counts sampling variation and is a Bonferroni-type lower bound for $\mu^{2}$ and hence for $R$, conservative relative to the size-corrected test $P(F>c\mid\mu^{2}=10)=0.05$.

In practice the $10\%$ maximal relative Nagar bias threshold for one instrument is therefore the Stock–Yogo size corrected value

$F^{*}\approx q_{0.95}[\chi^{2}_{1}(10)]\approx16.4$,

conventionally quoted as $F\gtrsim16$. On the integer scale this is $F\approx16$, essentially $16$–$17$, the $F>10$ mean rule lifted to the usual $5\%$ weak-instrument size.

The just identified homoskedastic Nagar first order is the one we actually use in practice

RelBias_N ≃ k2 μ^{-2}, k2=1,  E F1 =1+ μ² ,  
F1 →d χ²1(μ²)=[Z+√μ²]², √F1 ≃ N(√μ²,1)

on the mean scale RelBias ≃ μ^{-2} ≃ (E F-1)^{-1} ≃ F^{-1}.  
The point 10 % boundary is

R0=0.10 ⇔ μ0² = k2/R0 =10,  √μ0²≈3.162, E F0≈11,

the familiar F≈10 mean bias rule.

What is normally quoted as “95% confident that the asymptotic relative bias is <10%” is the size controlled weak instrument test

H0 : R ≥0.10 ⇔ H0 : μ² ≤ μ0² =10  vs  H1 : μ²>10

rejected at 5% size when F1>c with P_{μ²=10}[F1>c]=0.05.
In the ν2→∞ limit F1|μ²=10 → χ²1(10), so c is the 95th percentile of a non-central χ²1 with non-centrality 10, i.e. the 95th percentile of F1,∞(10).

c0.10 = q0.95[χ²1(10)] ≈ 16.38 ≈ 16–17

the Stock–Yogo 10% maximal relative bias critical value for L=1.  
An observed F>c rejects μ²≤10 at the conventional 5% level, which is the operational weak instrument meaning of “with 95% confidence the Nagar asymptotic relative 2SLS/OLS bias is <10%”. 
That is the F>10 point Nagar rule made 5% size correct, conventionally quoted as F≳16.

The √F ≈ N(√μ²,1) inversion √μ²L = √f – z1-α, μ²L=(√f–z)² and the requirement μ²L≥10 gives √f* = √10+z1-α, f*≈[√10+1.645]²≈23.1, ≈26.2 with z0.975. On the Nagar/Stock–Yogo calibration actually used in practice the 10% maximal relative bias threshold for one instrument is q0.95[χ²1(10)]≈16.4, conventionally quoted as F≈16. In round numbers that is the textbook weak instrument threshold for a 10% maximal relative Nagar bias.
